artists.biography:
The group was formed by guitarist, singer and chief songwriter Bill Fisher and keyboardist Michael Wetherburn over a mutual love of musical theatre and Queen. The group members had previously played in various bands in and around Nottingham, and a number of early songs by the group had been written years before while in other bands. Fisher was more interested in progressive pop rather than progressive rock, and wanted the band to be primarily about good songwriting over pointless technical ability. His influences include The Beatles, Kate Bush, David Bowie and Peter Gabriel, The instrumentation makes prominent use of the Hammond organ.

The band is signed to Bilocation Records. They have also covered Pink Floyd's "The Trial" on Magnetic Eye Records' tribute album The Wall Redux. Fisher has described the group as a "twofold entity: a new religious movement…and a 7-piece supergroup".

In 2017, the group released "Evil in your Eye" from their first album Is Satan Real? on 21 August to coincide with the solar eclipse on the same day.
Bill Fisher - guitar, vocals
Joanne Joyce - vocals
Caroline Cawley - vocals
Michael Wetherburn - keyboards, vocals
Amy Nicholson - cello, vocals
Sam Lloyd - bass
Loz Stone - drums

perplexity.description:
Is Satan Real? is the debut studio album by Church of the Cosmic Skull, released in 2016 via Bilocation Records. Hailing from Nottingham, the seven-piece band blends psychedelic rock, progressive elements, and lush vocal harmonies to create a sound that is both theatrical and introspective. The album features tracks such as "Mountain Heart," "Black Slug," and "Movements in the Sky," showcasing the band's penchant for layered instrumentation, melodic hooks, and a touch of theatrical flair. Their music draws comparisons to classic acts like Queen and Pink Floyd, while maintaining a distinct identity rooted in psychedelic and progressive rock traditions.

As the band's first full-length release, Is Satan Real? established Church of the Cosmic Skull as a unique voice in the modern rock scene. The album's themes explore existential questions, the nature of reality, and spiritual inquiry, all delivered with a sense of theatricality and sonic ambition. While major labels expressed interest, the band chose to maintain independence, releasing the album through Bilocation Records. The record received positive attention for its originality and musicianship, setting the stage for subsequent releases such as Science Fiction (2018) and Everybody's Going to Die (2019). Is Satan Real? remains a foundational work in their discography, marking the arrival of a band unafraid to blend rock, psychedelia, and philosophical inquiry.
